reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports all key premises regarding microstructural refinement, hardness increase, friction/wear reduction, and wear mechanism change, but only for the Al0.65CoCrFeNi alloy at room temperature. The hypothesis extends these findings to CoCrFeNi and to 800 °C without citing any high-temperature evidence, and the proposed mechanism of adaptive glaze layer formation is not supported by the cited passages.
premises: Laser remelting refines the microstructure of a CoCrFeNi-based HEA from coarse dendritic to submicron-scale basket-weave.
The refined basket-weave microstructure increases surface hardness.
The refined microstructure reduces friction coefficient by ~23% and wear rate by ~80% compared to the as-cast substrate.
The refined microstructure promotes a change in wear mechanism from adhesive/oxidative to abrasive, reducing adhesion.
